questions.question: How does the ‘homecoming’ become a redeployment in the story?
questions.solution_html:
• In state vs. non-state asymmetric warfare, the civilian population is the battlefield-When the
  • professional army cannot distinguish between a combatant and a civilian, the spatial boundaries of
  • war dissolve. - The conflict enters everyday spaces-markets, hospitals, and homes-becoming a
  • general social condition. - Guerrillas, insurgents, and terrorists do not wear uniforms or operate
  • from distinct military bases. They are deeply embedded within the populace
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: from distinct military bases. They are deeply embedded within the populace

questions.question: "Rifle was not merely a weapon; it was an extension of his body". Explain with reference to "Redeployment"

questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: battlefield-treating everyday life like an ongoing theatre of war.

questions.question: What is the significance of the kite and tail in the poem "If I must die"?
questions.solution_html:
• In military contexts, survival relies on an absolute, instinctive symbiosis between the soldier and
  • their weapon. The rifle ceases to be an external tool and becomes a vital sensory organ-totalizing
  • modern warfare is—shaping not just the soldier's ideology, but their physical posture and
  • psychological identity, making it difficult to shed the military identity.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: psychological identity, making it difficult to shed the military identity.

questions.question: Childhood in conflict zones-constant state of physical pain and fear. How does the father try to create memories for his son in "Sea prayer"?
questions.solution_html:
• Achille Mbembe expands upon Michel Foucault’s concept of biopower-the state’s power to "foster
  • life or disallow it to the point of death"-by shifting the analytical focus directly toward necropower
  • the sovereign power to dictate who may live and who must die-The war machine reduces human
  • bodies to disposable entities, enforcing total subjugation, transforming citizens into targets, and
  • turning entire regions into spaces where destruction is normalized and self-determination is
  • completely erased.
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026
questions.final_answer: completely erased.

questions.question: Discuss the role of memory and forgetting in "The End and the Beginning."

  • the perilous sea crossing ahead, the father uses the act of memory-keeping as an emotional
  • sanctuary.
